newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Reed-Elsevier to invest more in electronic media.
newsitem.headline: Reed-Elsevier to invest more in electronic media.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch publishing group Reed-Elsevier said on Thursday it planned to accelerate its investment in new product development and electronic publishing in the next few years.
In an end-of year trading statement the group said nearly one fifth of its revenues derived from electronic publishing in 1996 compared with very little five years ago.

This was partly due to the December 1994 acquisition of U.S. database operator Lexis-Nexis, but customer demand for information in electronic formats was developing rapidly and the pace of this trend was likely to pick up even further, it said.

"Being prepared for this change is our highest priority and we will accelerate our investment in new product development and electronic publishing infrastructures over the next couple of years to facilitate the transition," the statement said.

"The opportunities for Reed Elsevier are substantial; with our market leading franchises, the depth and quality of our content, and our considerable technology competencies we are positioned strongly to take full advantage of them," it added.
Reed-Elsevier's year-end statement coincided with a presentation on its electronic publishing activities to investors and analysts in London today.
